name: Shelomith
overview: Shelomith was a male member of the tribe of Levi, specifically a descendant of Izhar, as noted in 1 Chronicles 23:18. He belonged to the Izharite family, which descended from Kohath, the son of Levi. This lineage situates Shelomith within the priestly clan responsible for service in the tabernacle.
namesAndTitles: The name Shelomith, also rendered as Shelomoth, means 'at peace' in Hebrew. This proper name, found in 1 Chronicles 23:18 and 24:22, was not given by God but reflects a peaceful attribute associated with the individual.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Shelomith as a descendant of Izhar and infers that his father was Jahath, according to 1 Chronicles 24:22. These relationships place him within the Izharite branch of the Levites, but no further family details are recorded.
scriptureSignificance: Shelomith's significance lies in his role as part of the Levitical lineage descending from Izhar, which was important for the organization and duties of the priestly families. His mention in the genealogical records underscores the careful preservation of Levitical heritage and the continuity of priestly service in Israel. This contributes to the broader biblical narrative emphasizing the sanctity and order of God's chosen priesthood.
